tools.name: getfly_list_users
tools.description: List the Getfly CRM users (employees): user id, name, department, email, phone. Use the user_name (login name) for the recipient/manager arguments of the create tools. Filters: user_id, contact_name, email, contact_mobile, valid (1 = active users). GET /api/v6.1/users.

tools.name: getfly_get_user
tools.description: One user by id or by login name (exactly one of user_id and user_username). GET /api/v6.1/user.

tools.name: getfly_list_accounts
tools.description: List customers (accounts, i.e. companies or individuals) with code, name, phone, email, address, type, source, relationship, manager, total revenue and contacts. Filters: id, account_code, account_name, phone_office, email, account_type, account_source, relation_id, industry, billing_address_street,

tools.name: getfly_get_account
tools.description: One customer by its customer code (account_code, e.g. KH/2025/000001): full profile with contacts, custom fields, type, source, industry, manager and revenue. GET /api/v6.1/account?account_code=.

tools.name: getfly_create_account
tools.description: WRITE: Create a new customer (account) in Getfly CRM. The customer code must be unique (leave it out to let Getfly generate one). Type, source, industry, relationship, country, province, district and ward are given by NAME and must match the names configured in Getfly. Optionally adds one primary co

tools.name: getfly_update_account
tools.description: WRITE: Update fields of an existing customer, found by its current customer code. Send only the fields to change. Names (relationship, country, province...) must match those configured in Getfly. Contacts and the type/source/industry lists are not editable here. PUT /api/v6.1/account.

tools.name: getfly_list_campaigns
tools.description: List sales campaigns (opportunity pipelines): campaign code and name, responsible user, lock state, related users and the pipeline stages (status ids and names). GET /api/v6.1/campaigns.

tools.name: getfly_get_campaign_stages
tools.description: The pipeline stages of one campaign (status id, name and how many opportunities are in each). Pass exactly one of campaign_id and campaign_code. GET /api/v6.1/campaign/status.

tools.name: getfly_list_opportunities
tools.description: List sales opportunities (deals in a campaign pipeline) with code, name, stage, probability, handler, customer and campaign. Filter by campaign with the campaign_code argument. GET /api/v6.1/opportunities.

tools.name: getfly_get_opportunity
tools.description: One opportunity by its code (e.g. CH2284): stage, probability, handler, customer and campaign. GET /api/v6.1/opportunity.

tools.name: getfly_list_opportunity_comments
tools.description: The discussion (comments) on an opportunity: author, text and time. GET /api/v6.1/opportunity/{id}/comments.

tools.name: getfly_create_opportunity
tools.description: WRITE: Create a sales opportunity in a campaign for a customer and assign it to a user. Creates (or links) the customer and contact from the details given. The assigned user and the campaign rules may be notified by Getfly. POST /api/v6.1/opportunity.

tools.name: getfly_move_opportunity_stage
tools.description: WRITE: Move an opportunity to another stage of its campaign pipeline, without changing anything else. Identify the opportunity by code (or id) and the campaign by code (or id); the new stage by name (or status id) from getfly_get_campaign_stages. Won/lost/cancelled results are not set here. PUT /api

tools.name: getfly_add_opportunity_comment
tools.description: WRITE: Post a comment in the discussion of an opportunity, as the given user. Other users following the opportunity may be notified. POST /api/v6.1/opportunity/{id}/comments.

tools.name: getfly_list_products
tools.description: List products and services with code, name, category, unit, retail/wholesale/online price, sale price, VAT and dates. GET /api/v6.1/products.

tools.name: getfly_get_product
tools.description: One product by its code (e.g. SP.00192): prices, unit, category, VAT, variants and custom fields. GET /api/v6.1/product.

tools.name: getfly_list_sale_orders
tools.description: List sales orders with code, customer, amounts, discount, VAT, status, payment status, assigned user and line items. Filters: id, order_date, created_at, updated_at (eq, gte, lte, between). Newest first. GET /api/v6.1/sale_orders.

tools.name: getfly_get_sale_order
tools.description: One sales order by its order code: status, payment status, amounts, customer, line items, shipping info and custom fields. Add payment_periods to fields to include the payment schedule. GET /api/v6.1/sale_order.

tools.name: getfly_list_tickets
tools.description: List support tickets with code, title, content, category, customer and custom fields. GET /api/v6.1/tickets.

tools.name: getfly_get_ticket
tools.description: One support ticket by its ticket code. GET /api/v6.1/ticket.

tools.name: getfly_list_ticket_comments
tools.description: The discussion (comments) on a support ticket: author, text and time. GET /api/v6.1/ticket/{id}/comments.

tools.name: getfly_list_ticket_categories
tools.description: The support ticket categories (id and name). Use a name as cate_name when creating a ticket. GET /api/v6.1/ticket/categories.

tools.name: getfly_list_ticket_statuses
tools.description: The support ticket statuses (id and name). Use a name as status_name when creating a ticket. GET /api/v6.1/ticket/status.

tools.name: getfly_create_ticket
tools.description: WRITE: Create a support ticket, optionally for a customer. Category and status are given by NAME and must match the names configured in Getfly (getfly_list_ticket_categories, getfly_list_ticket_statuses). The content may contain HTML. Getfly may notify the support team. POST /api/v6.1/ticket.

tools.name: getfly_list_tasks
tools.description: List tasks with code, name, start/end time, status, progress, assignee, project and related customers. GET /api/v6.1/tasks.

tools.name: getfly_get_task
tools.description: One task by its task code: status, progress, assignee, project, dates and custom fields. GET /api/v6.1/task.

tools.name: getfly_create_task
tools.description: WRITE: Create a task, optionally in a project, assigned to a user and linked to a customer. Project and task type are given by NAME and must exist in Getfly; users by login name. The assignee may be notified by Getfly. POST /api/v6.1/task.

tools.name: getfly_complete_task
tools.description: WRITE: Mark a task as completed, by its task code. POST /api/v6.1/task/complete.

tools.name: getfly_list_funds
tools.description: List the cash/bank funds (accounts for receipts and payments) with id, name, parent, level and financial account. GET /api/v6.1/funds.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: getfly_list_users, getfly_list_accounts, getfly_list_opportunity_comments, getfly_list_tickets, getfly_get_ticket, getfly_list_ticket_comments, getfly_list_ticket_categories, getfly_list_ticket_statuses · Private data: getfly_list_accounts, getfly_get_account, getfly_create_account, getfly_update_account, getfly_create_opportunity · Public sink: getfly_list_users, getfly_list_accounts, getfly_create_account, getfly_update_account, getfly_create_opportunity, getfly_add_opportunity_comment, getfly_create_ticket, getfly_create_task, getfly_complete_task.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: getfly_list_users, getfly_list_accounts, getfly_list_opportunity_comments, getfly_list_tickets, getfly_get_ticket, getfly_list_ticket_comments, getfly_list_ticket_categories, getfly_list_ticket_statuses · Private data: getfly_list_accounts, getfly_get_account, getfly_create_account, getfly_update_account, getfly_create_opportunity · Public sink: getfly_list_users, getfly_list_accounts, getfly_create_account, getfly_update_account, getfly_create_opportunity, getfly_add_opportunity_comment, getfly_create_ticket, getfly_create_task, getfly_complete_task

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
